definition: Your AI Slop Bores Me (stylized in all lowercase and abbreviated as YASBM) is a website and social experiment created by programmer Mihir Maroju.
details: Serving as a parody of large language models (LLMs) like ChatGPT and Claude, all questions and image prompts posed by users are answered by other, randomly-selected human users of the site. As of March 2026, the site had reached 50 million hits and sustained approximately 16,000 concurrent users.

explainer.lead: Your AI Slop Bores Me is a website and social experiment by programmer Mihir Maroju that parodies large language models. Every question and image prompt is answered by a randomly selected human user instead of a model.

tiers.eli5: It looks like a chatbot, but a random person on the internet types the reply, not a computer.
tiers.practitioner: It is a social experiment, not a deployable model, so its value is as a comparison point for AI answers. A pitfall for anyone studying it is that human replies are slow and inconsistent compared with model output.
tiers.paperLevel: No formal definition applies; it is a human-in-the-loop parody of LLM interfaces, and its known limit is throughput tied to the number of available human respondents.

explainer.example: As of March 2026 the site had reached 50 million hits and sustained about 16,000 concurrent users answering prompts by hand.
